title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires AI developers and users in China to submit detailed reports on their AI systems’ capabilities and usage to government regulators. This law aims to promote transparency, monitor AI development, and ensure the technology aligns with national safety and policy objectives.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is legislation that prohibits the use of artificial intelligence as medical practitioners, ensuring that only licensed human doctors can diagnose, treat and prescribe. It aims to protect patient safety and maintain professional standards by limiting AI involvement in direct patient care.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, tasked with identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks from AI and other emerging technologies. The office will coordinate across agencies, develop guidelines, and advise the President on related policy and regulatory matters.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to establish a federal framework that promotes safe and trustworthy AI development by setting standards for reliability, transparency, and accountability in AI research and deployment. It encourages collaboration between government agencies, academia, and industry to ensure that AI systems are rigorously tested, ethically designed, and aligned with societal values before they are released to the public.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes guidelines for managing risks associated with AI and enhances security measures to protect against potential threats. It requires organizations to assess AI systems’ safety and compliance, and sets penalties for non‑compliance.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to oversee the secure deployment of AI technologies. It aims to coordinate federal efforts to mitigate AI‑related risks, develop best practices, and ensure that AI systems comply with national security and privacy standards.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to investigate incidents where artificial intelligence systems create or exacerbate cybersecurity threats. The board will oversee investigations, recommend policy changes, and coordinate responses to help keep AI technologies safe and secure.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to examine and shape policy surrounding AI. The committee will review AI developments, recommend regulations, and guide responsible use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 proposes a framework for assessing and managing the risks associated with AI systems. It aims to establish guidelines, standards, and oversight mechanisms to ensure safe, reliable, and ethical deployment of AI technology.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate artificial intelligence, ensuring that AI systems are developed and used safely, transparently, and responsibly. It aims to set standards, establish risk‑assessment procedures, and create oversight mechanisms to protect public interests while encouraging innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction of new data centers specifically designed for AI workloads, aiming to reduce environmental impact and encourage more sustainable technologies. It also encourages investment in energy‑efficient infrastructure and stricter regulatory oversight for existing AI data centers.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules to curb the environmental footprint of AI systems. It requires companies to measure and report AI‑related emissions, invest in greener infrastructure, and pursue research that makes AI models more energy‑efficient.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that benefit American citizens and the economy. It establishes policies for transparency, accountability, and equitable access to AI tools, with the goal of preventing harm and maximizing public good.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires schools to embed AI education into their curricula so students gain foundational knowledge and critical thinking skills about artificial intelligence. It also mandates teacher training, resource allocation, and equity measures to ensure every student can responsibly engage with AI technologies.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 establishes national standards and oversight mechanisms to ensure that AI research and development produce systems that are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values. The act requires rigorous testing, documentation, and accountability measures for AI researchers and organizations to promote reliability and public trust.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, working through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence for defending critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes other related actions to support this initiative.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students from kindergarten through high school with foundational knowledge and critical skills for understanding and responsibly using artificial intelligence. It establishes national standards, curriculum resources, and teacher training programs to ensure schools can integrate AI education and prepare students for a technology‑driven future.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to ensure that artificial‑intelligence tools used in Veterans Affairs claims are transparent, reliable, and accountable. It requires regular audits, oversight mechanisms, and safeguards to protect veterans' rights and prevent bias in automated decision‑making.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how it develops and deploys artificial intelligence systems. It mandates reporting on AI risk assessments, data sources, and impact on veteran services to ensure accountability and protect patient privacy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a nationwide campaign to increase public understanding of artificial intelligence, covering its benefits, risks, and potential impacts. It establishes funding, guidelines, and partnerships to provide clear, accessible information and educational resources to all citizens.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate has issued a resolution that stresses the importance of protecting religious freedom in the development and use of artificial intelligence. It also calls for AI systems to be built on authoritative texts and to maintain transparency so that their operations remain clear and accountable.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act requires companies to clearly label any content created by AI and to disclose when AI is being used in products or services. It also sets penalties for deceptive AI practices and establishes a consumer protection framework to ensure that people can reliably identify and trust AI-generated information.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress. That report will cover how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to strengthen AI education and equip the workforce with the skills needed for emerging AI roles. It likely supports updated curricula, expanded training programs, and career pathways to ensure readiness for the AI‑driven economy.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act seeks to promote and regulate the development of open-source artificial intelligence technologies, encouraging transparency, collaboration, and shared innovation across the industry. By providing guidelines, incentives, and safeguards for open-source AI projects, the act aims to reduce monopolistic control, protect user privacy, and ensure that AI systems are developed responsibly and ethically.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is designed to prevent AI companies from charging excessively high prices for their services and from fixing or manipulating wages for workers. It would create rules and penalties that enforce fair pricing and equitable pay across the AI industry.
